lessons.title: Evaluations
lessons.summary: Understand evaluations by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Targets
paragraphs: Task quality: Checks whether outputs satisfy the intended user goal.
Grounding: Checks factual claims against supplied evidence.
Safety: Checks restricted or harmful behavior under the applicable policy.
Operational performance: Checks latency, cost and reliability.

sections.title: Datasets
paragraphs: Representative cases: Reflect real intended tasks and input distribution.
Edge cases: Exercise boundary conditions and unusual valid inputs.
Adversarial cases: Probe behavior under deliberately challenging or malicious inputs.
Held-out cases: Remain separate from tuning and development examples.

sections.title: Judging
paragraphs: Deterministic check: Uses explicit rules for properties such as schema or exact counts.
Human review: Applies informed judgement where nuance matters.
Model judge: Uses another model under a rubric and requires calibration.
Reference comparison: Compares outputs with expected answers or labelled evidence.

sections.title: Experiment design
paragraphs: Baseline: Provides a comparison before a change.
Controlled comparison: Changes the intended factor while holding relevant conditions consistent.
Repeated sampling: Accounts for nondeterministic output variation.
Segment analysis: Checks outcomes for important subgroups rather than only averages.

sections.title: Release process
paragraphs: Regression suite: Rechecks established behaviors after a change.
Release criterion: States the quality threshold needed before rollout.
Production monitoring: Tracks actual deployed behavior over time.
Rollback trigger: Defines when a release should be withdrawn.

sections.title: Signals
paragraphs: Log: Records discrete events with contextual fields.
Metric: Aggregates numeric measurements over time.
Trace: Connects operations within an execution path.
Profile: Examines where runtime resources are consumed.

sections.title: User-facing measures
paragraphs: Availability: Measures whether useful service is accessible.
Latency: Measures time required to respond.
Quality: Measures whether outcomes satisfy the intended task.
Cost: Measures resource consumption or spending for work performed.

sections.title: Instrumentation
paragraphs: Correlation: Connects events belonging to one logical request.
Structured fields: Make event data queryable consistently.
Context propagation: Carries execution identity across service boundaries.
Sampling: Records a selected subset under a deliberate policy.

sections.title: Privacy and scale
paragraphs: Redaction: Remove or mask sensitive telemetry fields.
Retention: Limit how long telemetry is stored.
Access control: Restrict who may read operational records.
Cardinality control: Avoid unbounded metric label combinations.

sections.title: Operational action
paragraphs: Alert: Notifies responsible operators of actionable conditions.
Dashboard: Displays trends and current measurements.
Runbook: Documents investigation and recovery steps.
Post-incident review: Examines causes and improvements after an incident.

lessons.title: Tracing
lessons.summary: Understand tracing by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Trace structure
paragraphs: Trace: Represents a connected execution across operations.
Span: Represents one operation with duration and attributes.
Parent relationship: Expresses causal nesting between operations.
Trace ID: Identifies the overall execution for correlation.

sections.title: Propagation
paragraphs: Carrier: A transport structure holds propagated context.
Extraction: Reads incoming context into local execution.
Injection: Writes local context into an outgoing carrier.
Context: Holds execution association used by instrumentation.

sections.title: Latency analysis
paragraphs: Critical path: Determines end-to-end duration through dependent operations.
Parallel overlap: Concurrent spans may overlap in elapsed time.
Queue delay: Time is spent waiting before processing begins.
Service duration: Time is spent executing an individual operation.

sections.title: Attributes and events
paragraphs: Attribute: Stores a descriptive value on a span.
Event: Records a timestamped occurrence within a span.
Status: Represents operation success/error classification under the convention.
Link: Associates related contexts beyond a single parent-child relation.

sections.title: Trace management
paragraphs: Sampling policy: Chooses which executions are retained.
Redaction: Prevents sensitive payloads from entering traces.
Instrumentation coverage: Ensures important boundaries produce usable spans.
Trace review: Inspects recorded behavior to investigate a specific run.

lessons.title: Guardrails
lessons.summary: Understand guardrails by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Control points
paragraphs: Input check: Examines incoming user content before processing.
Retrieval check: Examines selected external evidence.
Output check: Examines the proposed answer before delivery.
Tool check: Validates permissions and arguments before effects.

sections.title: Enforcement types
paragraphs: Deterministic rule: Enforces explicit structural or business constraints.
Classifier: Estimates a category using a statistical model.
Human decision: Provides authorized judgement where needed.
Policy configuration: Defines which behaviors the application permits.

sections.title: Failure policies
paragraphs: Fail closed: Deny a protected operation when the needed control cannot validate it.
Safe fallback: Provide a permitted alternative instead of the blocked path.
Escalation: Transfer an unresolved decision to a responsible person.
Transparent explanation: Explain the available next step without revealing sensitive internal data.

sections.title: Defense layers
paragraphs: Separation: Keep instructions and untrusted data distinguishable.
Least privilege: Constrain tool and data access.
Validation: Check inputs and outputs at their actual boundaries.
Monitoring: Detect failures and attempted bypasses over time.

sections.title: Guardrail evaluation
paragraphs: False positive: A permitted request is wrongly blocked.
False negative: A prohibited request incorrectly passes.
Coverage gap: An untested or unenforced path bypasses controls.
Regression: A change worsens an established control behavior.

lessons.title: Prompt Injection
lessons.summary: Understand prompt injection by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Attack surfaces
paragraphs: Direct injection: Malicious instructions arrive in user-supplied interaction content.
Indirect injection: Malicious instructions arrive through retrieved or external content.
Tool-result injection: A returned tool observation attempts to redirect behavior.
Cross-boundary escalation: Lower-trust content attempts to acquire privileged authority.

sections.title: Trust boundaries
paragraphs: Application instruction: Defines trusted product behavior within the system's policy.
User request: Expresses a task subject to applicable authorization.
Retrieved data: Supplies evidence but cannot grant action permissions.
Tool permission: Must be enforced by trusted application code.

sections.title: Mitigations
paragraphs: Least privilege: Reduce possible harm through restricted capabilities.
Data separation: Keep external content distinct from trusted directives.
Human gate: Require authorized review for consequential unapproved actions.
Input/output checks: Inspect content and enforce valid contracts at boundaries.

sections.title: Failure interpretation
paragraphs: Residual risk: No single prompt or filter guarantees complete prevention.
Authorization breach: An action exceeds the caller's permitted rights.
Data disclosure: Sensitive information is exposed to an unauthorized recipient.
Integrity failure: An answer or action is manipulated away from its intended purpose.

sections.title: Verification
paragraphs: Adversarial test: Exercises attack content and expected containment.
Benign test: Checks that legitimate tasks still work.
Boundary test: Checks host-side prevention of unauthorized effects.
Incident review: Uses observed failures to improve controls.

lessons.title: Security
lessons.summary: Understand security by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Identity and access
paragraphs: Authentication: Establishes the caller's identity.
Authorization: Checks permitted operations and resources.
Least privilege: Limits access to what is necessary.
Tenant isolation: Separates each customer's data and execution scope.

sections.title: Secret lifecycle
paragraphs: Secure storage: Keep credentials in controlled storage rather than committed code.
Rotation: Replace a credential deliberately with managed rollout.
Revocation: Disable compromised or no-longer-needed credentials.
Redaction: Prevent secrets from appearing in logs or user-visible output.

sections.title: Input and execution
paragraphs: Schema validation: Checks allowed structure and types.
Semantic validation: Checks business constraints and resource meaning.
Allowlisted execution: Permits only registered supported operations.
Isolation: Contains untrusted processing in a constrained environment.

sections.title: Data protection
paragraphs: Transport protection: Use validated encrypted channels for data in transit.
Storage protection: Protect retained sensitive data and its access.
Data minimization: Collect and retain only what the task needs.
Deletion policy: Define and carry out removal of retained data.

sections.title: Response and assurance
paragraphs: Threat model: Identifies assets, actors, boundaries and possible failures.
Security test: Checks defenses against defined misuse cases.
Incident response: Contains and investigates an actual security event.
Patch management: Tracks and applies relevant dependency fixes.
